h1: The 8 Best TV Stands on Wheels of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best TV Stands on Wheels 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight rolling TV stands compared on TV size range, weight rating, locking wheels, VESA support and tip-over stability.
summary: The TVON Heavy Duty cart is the best rolling TV stand, with all four wheels locking, a built-in 4-outlet 12A power strip and a 110 lb rating for 32 to 83 inch TVs. The Perlegear has the widest base, the 15-step cart suits offices, and the Mount-It! adds a webcam tray. The PERLESMITH reaches 85 inches, the FITUEYES rotates to portrait, and the 250 lb cart handles 120 inch displays.
intro: Rolling TV stands get chosen by screen size and judged on everything but the wheels. The detail that decides whether one is safe is how many casters lock and how wide the base is, because a tall mast carrying a heavy set pushes the center of gravity high, and a narrow footprint with free-rolling wheels will tip if a child pulls on it.

Eight rolling carts went through our listing review, and the Primea score put locking wheels, base width, weight rating, VESA support and extras like power or camera shelves at the top of the weighting. Prices appear as buckets only. Check your TV's weight, diagonal and VESA pattern first, because all three have to fit before any ranking helps.

products.name: TVON Heavy Duty Rolling TV Stand with Power Outlet, 32-83 Inch
products.verdict: All four wheels lock, and a 12A outlet strip is built in.
products.description:
The TVON fits 32 to 83 inch TVs up to 110 lbs, adjusts from 44 to 65 inches and supports VESA 100x100mm to 600x400mm. It adds a 4-outlet, 12A power strip and cable management, and sells in the $50 to $100 bracket. A built-in strip means one cord to the wall, which tidies a rolling setup.

It beats the other 110 lb carts because all four wheels lock, while the 15-step cart brakes only two of four casters. The Perlegear has a wider base but costs more and lacks the strip.

Buy it for family rooms with kids and pets. The caveats are no camera tray and no support for 85 inch screens. Skip it if you need a webcam shelf.
products.idealFor: Family rooms with kids and pets.

products.name: Perlegear Rolling TV Stand for 32-84 Inch TV, Heavy-Duty Base
products.verdict: The widest base in the roundup, with a safety screw backup.
products.description:
The Perlegear fits 32 to 84 inch TVs up to 100 lbs, with 11 height levels, a 29.34 by 23.14 inch base, a cold-rolled steel frame and a safety screw backup. Its rubber wheels suit hardwood and carpet. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket. A wide base lowers the tipping risk because the footprint extends further under the load.

It ranks second because the base is the widest in the roundup, but it costs a bracket more than the TVON and lists a lower weight rating. The safety screw adds a backup against the TV sliding off.

Buy it for tip-over-conscious households. The caveats are the larger floor footprint and the higher price. Skip it if floor space is tight.

products.name: Mobile TV Stand Rolling TV Cart with Lockable Wheels, 32-83 Inch
products.verdict: Fast assembly and 15 height steps at a mid price.
products.description:
This cart fits 32 to 83 inch TVs up to 110 lbs, adjusts from 44 to 64 inches in 15 steps, supports VESA up to 600x400mm and uses a space-saving base. Two of its four casters have brakes. It is in the $50 to $100 bracket. Fifteen height steps let you set the screen more precisely than the 11-level Perlegear allows.

It ranks below the TVON because only two casters brake and there is no power strip, though the capacity matches. Fast assembly suits offices and schools that deploy many units.

Buy it for offices and schools. The caveats are that only two wheels lock and no power strip is included. Skip it if you want all wheels locked.

products.name: Mount-It! Tall Mobile TV Cart for 37-70 Inch TVs with Camera Tray
products.verdict: A dual shelf, webcam tray and lifetime warranty.
products.description:
The Mount-It! fits 37 to 70 inch TVs up to 110 lbs, tilts 10 degrees each way, has two locking casters, a dual shelf plus webcam tray and VESA up to 600x400mm. It carries a lifetime warranty and costs in the $100 to $200 bracket. A camera tray holds a webcam level with the screen, which is the point of a conference cart.

It ranks fourth because the TV range is narrower than the others and only two casters lock. The tilt helps with glare in a meeting room, and the lifetime warranty is the strongest coverage in the guide.

Buy it for video calls and presentations. The caveats are the narrower TV range and two locking casters. Skip it if your TV is over 70 inches.

products.name: PERLESMITH Rolling TV Stand with Wheels for 32-85 Inch TVs
products.verdict: Handles up to 85 inch TVs with tilt and internal cable routing.
products.description:
The PERLESMITH fits 32 to 85 inch TVs up to 100 lbs, with 39.37 to 59.06 inch height, lockable casters, tilt of minus 10 and plus 5 degrees, internal cable routing and both camera and A/V shelves. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket. Internal cable routing hides cords inside the mast.

Fifth place reflects a lower maximum height and a lower weight rating than the 110 lb carts. It beats the Mount-It! on screen range, reaching 85 inches, and it adds the shelves.

Buy it for large-screen buyers. The caveats are the lower max height and the higher price bracket. Skip it if you want a taller mast.

products.name: Mobile TV Stand with Upgraded Wheels for 32-75 Inch TVs
products.verdict: The straightforward budget stand for bedrooms and living rooms.
products.description:
This stand takes 32 to 75 inch screens weighing up to 88 lbs, adjusts from 44 to 56 inches, locks its front wheels and supports VESA 100x100mm to 400x400mm. It has a middle AV shelf and cable management, in the $50 to $100 bracket. Locking only the front wheels leaves the rears free, which is a trade at this price.

It ranks sixth because the 88 lb rating and partial wheel locking trail the stronger carts. It matches the price bucket of the TVON but offers less.

Buy it for bedrooms and light TVs. The caveats are the lower 88 lb rating and only front wheels locking. Skip it if your TV is heavy.

products.name: FITUEYES Rolling TV Stand with Landscape to Portrait Rotation
products.verdict: The only stand here that rotates to portrait.
products.description:
The FITUEYES handles 32 to 75 inch screens at 88 lbs, rotates from landscape to portrait, swivels 40 degrees and locks all wheels. It has an iron base and rear cable management, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Portrait mode suits signage, menus and creative displays that a normal cart cannot manage.

It ranks seventh because the rotation is a specialty feature, and the 88 lb limit and price put it behind the general-purpose carts. It is the only stand here that rotates.

Buy it for creators and displays. The caveats are the 88 lb limit and the higher price bracket. Skip it if you just want a TV stand.
products.skipIf: You just want a TV stand.

products.name: Heavy Duty Mobile TV Cart for 55-120 Inch TVs, Holds Up to 250 lbs
products.verdict: The only cart rated for 120 inch and 250 lb displays.
products.description:
This cart fits 55 to 120 inch TVs up to 250 lbs, supports VESA up to 800x600mm, uses locking swivel casters and has a height-adjustable 44 lb shelf on a wide welded steel base. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket. Welded steel and a wide base are what let it carry a screen this heavy.

It ranks last only because it is overkill for homes and the most expensive. No other cart here comes close on capacity.

Buy it for commercial large displays. The caveats are the top price bracket and the bulk. Skip it if you have a typical TV.

whatMatters.detail: Casters with brakes keep the cart still. A cart with only two locking wheels can still creep, especially on hardwood. Check the listing for how many lock, and favor all four if kids or pets are near, since a rolling stand that moves under a bump is a safety risk. Test the locks by rocking the cart after assembly.

The rating is the heaviest TV the cart is rated for. Check your TV's weight in its manual, and leave headroom, since a rating near the TV's weight leaves no margin. Add the weight of any soundbar or shelf gear you plan to load. Weight ratings here run from 88 lb on the budget stand to 250 lb on the commercial cart.

VESA is the bolt pattern on the back of the TV. If your pattern is larger than the cart supports, it will not fit. Check the numbers, like 600x400mm, against your TV's manual, and remember large TVs often use bigger patterns than carts list. The pattern is usually in the TV's spec sheet or on the back panel.

A wide base resists tipping. Compare base dimensions, like 29.34 by 23.14 inches, with your floor space, and note that a wider base needs more room around it. Safety backups, like the Perlegear's screw, help if the TV is bumped. Place heavy items low and keep cords from snagging.

Eye level depends on your seating. Check the minimum and maximum mast height, and note the adjustment steps, since 15 steps give finer control than 11. A low mast suits bedrooms, while a tall one suits standing presentations. Seated viewers want the center of the screen near eye height.

faq.a: Only if your TV size, weight and VESA pattern are within range. Check each listing, since the budget stand tops out at 75 inches and 88 lb. Pair the pattern, weight and diagonal before buying. A cart that fits two of the three still fails.

Ignoring VESA. A TV with a larger pattern will not mount, however well the diagonal matches. Look up the pattern in your TV's manual, then compare it to the cart's maximum. The numbers are listed in millimeters.

faq.q: Is the Perlegear worth it over the TVON?
faq.a: If tip-over safety is your top worry, its wide base helps. Otherwise the TVON costs less and locks all wheels. Weigh floor space too, since the Perlegear's footprint is large.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: Assemble, mount the TV low on the mast first, then lock the wheels. Raise the height afterward with a helper, and re-check that every bolt is snug before you let anyone lean on the stand.

Check bolts every few months and keep wheels free of debris. Tighten the mast joints on the TVON or Perlegear if the stand begins to wobble, and clear hair or grit from the casters so the locks seat properly.

faq.q: Can I rotate my TV to portrait?
faq.a: Only the FITUEYES lists landscape to portrait rotation here, and it swivels 40 degrees as well. The 88 lb limit means check your screen's weight first, and secure the rotation lock before you move it.

finalTake: Buy the TVON for a family room with kids and pets, and the Perlegear if tip-over worries you most. The Mount-It! and PERLESMITH suit video calls and large screens, while the budget stand fits bedrooms with light TVs. Choose the FITUEYES for portrait signage and the 250 lb cart only for commercial displays. Always check weight rating and VESA pattern against your TV before ordering.
